newsitem.title: INDIA: High interest hurts India Nagarjuna net.
newsitem.headline: High interest hurts India Nagarjuna net.

text.p: Higher interest payments saw Nagarjuna Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd post a lower post-tax profit for the financial year ending March 31, 1997, the firm's chairman said on Thursday.
The firm, a leading urea producer from southern India, said it posted a net profit of 1.55 billion rupees for 1996/97 compared to 2.21 billion rupees in the previous year.
Interest payment during the year swelled to 1.43 billion rupees compared to 1.24 billion a year ago, the firm said.
"We withdrew money from investments to fund our expansion," Nagarjuna Fertilizers chairman Field Marshal S.H.F.J. Manekshaw told a news conference on Thursday.

Sales during 1996/97 grew to 9.22 billion rupees from 8.82 billion in the previous year, the firm said. Of this, 2.81 billion came from trading in products not made by the company, primarily imported urea, company officials said.
"Profits will be much higher next year, once it (expanded capacity) begins," Manekshaw said.
Nagarjuna produced 716,910 tonnes of urea during the year ending March 31, 1997. The company is doubling its capacity to 1.4 million tonnes in the first quarter of calendar 1998.
The 9.20-billion-rupee expansion is funded through internal accruals and loans, officials said.
